stem.en: White jasmine flowers look bright white. Why are their petals white and not coloured?

text.en: A white pigment called leucoplast, found in their plastids.

feedback.en: A leucoplast is a plastid, not a pigment, and it is colourless.

text.en: Chromoplasts, which hold a white pigment in most flowers.

feedback.en: Chromoplast pigments may be yellow, orange or red.

text.en: No coloured pigment: their plastids are colourless leucoplasts.

feedback.en: Yes. Leucoplasts are colourless, so they give the petal no colour.

text.en: Chlorophyll in the petal, which reflects all the white light that falls on it.

feedback.en: Chlorophyll is green. A white petal does not get its colour from it.

explanation.en: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids. A white petal gets no colour from them, because they hold no pigment.
